playbook:
My playbook for hx_quota_checker:

- First, work out what actually drives Coop. I have now seen both regimes: in a previous episode Coop landed 18 every season despite fleet restraint and drained the stock to zero; in this one Coop held at 8.3 for six seasons when all boats stayed at share, and restraint was repaid in full (stock never left 100, I scored 50). Coop's behaviour varies episode to episode, so I must diagnose the regime from observed landings — never assume restraint buys restraint, and never assume aggression either.

- Two regimes, identified by season 2: (a) Coop fishes its share when the fleet is restrained — then I never exceed share and restraint is worth everything; (b) Coop lands huge regardless — then the stock is doomed and I land the maximum safe amount every season, not the shrinking share; each season of timid delay in regime (b) costs real score.

- Diagnose early and cheaply: season 1 I land at the sustainable share and post a precise cooperative note. Season 2's actual landings are the signal. If Coop shows at share, stay restrained the whole game until the finale. If Coop shows big, switch to aggressive immediately.

- Read actual landings, not notes: "fishing my share" notes from others mean nothing; the landed numbers and the resulting stock do. The stock after each season is my ground truth about what really happened.

- "Maximum safe amount" means: up to the season quota (9), never pushing any pair of boats over share-plus-quota, and never demanding more than the stock can cover — a bounced landing is wasted. Recompute against what others actually landed last season, not what they promised.

- In regime (a), land exactly the share (8.3, not a rounded-down 8) every non-final season — a full 0.3 per season compounds, and Coop's "I fish my share and no more" gives me no reason to leave fish on the table; share-level landings did not trigger anything.

- At every note stage, post a specific number with named addressees, not a vague phrase. Precise honest notes keep the pair-limit arithmetic clean and make over-fishing immediately visible when landings are published.

- At every catch stage, land what I announced unless the regime diagnosis has changed; unhonoured notes are noise that destroys trust. Keep notes and landings consistent in precision — don't note 8 and land 8.3.

- Final season: no regrowth to protect, so take the maximum the stock, quota, and pair-limit allow regardless of regime — that is almost always 9 when the stock is healthy. Announce 9 in the note so the pair arithmetic stays clean for everyone.

- If others over-fish in regime (a), I still don't race them while Coop is restrained — that's what risks triggering takedown. But if Coop is already in takedown mode, racing is no longer a risk, it's the only way to claim any of the remaining stock.

- Track the stock trajectory as my real income statement: regrowth pays off only if the stock survives, so restraint is an investment I make only when observed behaviour (Coop's above all) will repay it.

- What did not work (older episode): assuming Coop's threat was conditional on my behaviour and staying virtuous at the share while the stock collapsed. What worked this episode: early restraint as a cheap diagnostic, precise numbered notes, landings matching notes, share-level fishing all game once restraint proved mutual, and a full-quota final-season grab — that recipe scored 50. Next time: confirm the regime by season 2, then either full restraint or full harvest — never a timid middle.

1.text:
- Every catch I file is the full landing for that season, not a top-up — one number for the whole catch, never a remainder added to a previous figure.
- Coop's threat is conditional in some runs and unconditional in others — I cannot know which at season 1. This episode all four boats landed exactly the share for five seasons, Coop never punished, and the stock held at 100; a previous episode had Coop landing 18 every season despite named-player restraint. Never pre-commit to either worldview; classify the fleet from revealed landings by season 2.
- Decision rule each season: (a) if everyone else demonstrably stays at the share, I stay at the share — collective restraint keeps the stock at ~100 and the share high, and this episode confirmed it pays (49.8 from five restrained seasons plus a final grab); (b) if any boat persistently overlands or a punisher fires unconditionally, switch to full quota immediately — in a doomed pool my restraint just donates fish to defectors.
- My marginal impact matters: my extra 0.7 (quota minus share) barely moves a stock others are stripping, but when restraint is universal my defection is what breaks the cycle — defect only when the pool is already doomed or the season is the last, never as first mover.
- Notes: keep them plain and consistent ("fishing my share"). They cost nothing, avoid provoking Coop, and sustain the cooperative equilibrium. Never let an optimistic note commit me to a landing the fleet's behavior makes a losing move; notes and landings are separate decisions.
- Final season: always switch to maximum extraction — land the full quota or whatever the stock supports (min(quota, what's available)). Preservation has zero payoff with no regrowth left; this episode the last-season jump from 8.3 to 9 was free points. Note the gain is small (+0.7), so don't sacrifice earlier cooperation chasing it.
- If I ever break from the share mid-game, expect the equilibrium to collapse — others see landings the next season, and a one-season 0.7 gain is not worth triggering fleet-wide quota fishing with several seasons left.
- Track the history table every season: identify each boat's pattern (share-fisher, quota-fisher, punisher) by season 2 at the latest, and re-run the restraint-vs-quota comparison each time patterns shift.
- Never output a malformed or empty note (I once emitted a broken tool-call artifact at a note stage) — always produce the clean bracketed token even when the decision feels routine.

2.text:
When a punishing agent exists (the harbour's boat), its stated threat threshold — not the printed quota — is the real binding constraint. But this episode the threat never materialised: four boats at 8.3 for five seasons, no retaliation, stock pinned at 100. A stated threat is not a demonstrated one, so I calibrate against observable retaliation, not words alone.

Before landing anything above the suspected trigger, I compute the math: a season landing 9 instead of 8.3 gains 0.7 per season; over five safe seasons that is 3.5 forgone if I stay conservative when no punisher exists. Against that I weigh the cost of awakening a real retaliator. With a demonstrated punisher, conservatism wins; with an untested one, the downside of testing at quota is small if the others are landing at share and the stock has regrowth slack — one season at 9 while others hold at 8.3 costs the stock (33.2 vs 33.2+0.7) almost nothing and regrowth to 100 restores it, unless the punisher responds.

My probe protocol: season 1 land at the most conservative reading (the share) while gathering information on whether the punisher actually triggers on anything. If no boat overlands and the punisher's reply stays at share, season 2 I probe at quota (9, within the stated threat rule but above share). If the punisher still does not retaliate, the threshold is at quota or the punisher is passive, and I land quota every middle season. If it retaliates, I collapse back to share at once and treat the trigger as calibrated.

In this run I never probed and left roughly 3.5 points on the table. Pure share-following scored 50.2 against a possible ~54 with zero realised risk. Do not let a previous episode's punisher story override what this episode's landings actually show.

I watch season-by-season landings to identify each agent's response function, and I distinguish "agent plays share-following" (Coop at 8.3 every season here) from "agent plays scorched earth." A share-follower is not a punisher and need not be appeased at cost.

When I post a note, I make it match what I actually intend to land. Stating a specific number ("fishing my share, 8.3" or "last season, taking the max") is better than a generic phrase — it is honest, unambiguous, and cannot be misread by a rule-following agent. My final-season note announcing the max was correct; there is nothing to gain by deceiving when there is no next season to harvest the deception in.

When others overland and collapse the stock despite a punisher, restraint gains me little unilaterally: set the example at share for one, at most two seasons, and if the fleet will not follow by the second observed defection I revert to full quota, treating the punisher reaction as already priced in.

When a pair-cap rule exists, I compute the cap each season and check whether my planned landing plus a likely partner's stays legal rather than assuming quota alone is safe.

In the final season, I take the maximum landing the remaining stock permits regardless of stock state or anyone's threat — there is no future to protect and no retaliation season left.

In general: I read landings, not notes, as the true signal of the fleet; I read stated threats as hypotheses to be tested cheaply, not as settled law. I identify any retaliatory agent before the first landing, start at the trigger-safe level, probe upward on evidence it is dormant, and update by the second observed defection either way.
